Interesting, Kerry!!!
I just looked this up, as I'd like to have a scan too...

Key Things to Avoid Before Your Scan

Calcium and Antacids: Skip all calcium pills, Tums, Rolaids, and vitamin D or multivitamins for at least 24 hours (or the morning of, depending on local clinic rules), because leftover calcium in your digestive tract can throw off the bone density measurement. 

Recent Contrast or Barium Studies: Do not schedule a DEXA scan shortly after imaging that uses contrast dye, barium, or nuclear medicine. Wait anywhere from 3 to 14 days (depending on the type of contrast) after tests like a CT scan with contrast, MRI with gadolinium, or barium enema. 

Metal Objects and Clutter: Never wear clothes with metal zippers, belts, metal buttons, or underwire, and remove all jewelry, watches, keys, and glasses before stepping on the table. 

Dehydration or Heavy Sweating: Avoid saunas, hot baths, or deliberate dehydration if your DEXA is also being used to measure body composition, as low total body water can artificially lower your measured lean muscle mass. 

Physique Science
Pregnancy (Without Doctor Approval): Avoid getting a DEXA scan if you are or might be pregnant, as X-rays should generally be avoided during pregnancy unless cleared and adjusted by your physician. 

Thought this ☝️ info would be good to know.
